```plato
    //==
    // # Environmental force models — the ForceOn bodies
    //
    // What each declared model actually exerts. Every one is a force in newtons on
    // the body as it currently stands, so a caller sums them and hands the total
    // to the integrator; none of them mutates or schedules anything.
    //
    // `BuoyancyModel` has no `ForceOn` here and does not claim `IForceModel3D`.
    // Buoyancy is minus the weight of the DISPLACED FLUID, and the displaced
    // volume is a shape query against the fluid half-space — a `RigidBody3D`
    // carries no shape, so the interface cannot supply the one number the force
    // depends on. `BuoyantForce` below takes that volume as an argument instead of
    // pretending to derive it.

    // Weight: the same acceleration on every body, scaled by its mass and its own
    // gravity multiplier. Static and kinematic bodies are not exempted here —
    // `SolverBody3D` exempts them by having no inverse mass, and a caller working
    // in `RigidBody3D` reads the motion kind through `MobilityScale`.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravity_of_Earth)
    ForceOn(self: UniformGravity2D, body: RigidBody2D): Vector2D
        => self.Acceleration * (body.MassProperties.Mass.Amount * body.GravityScale);
```

## Line 132

**Source:** [stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato, line 132](../../../../../stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato#L132).

```plato

    // Newtonian attraction toward a point mass: magnitude mu * m / r^2, directed
    // from the body toward the centre. A body AT the centre has no direction to
    // fall in and feels nothing, which keeps the singularity out of the caller.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton%27s_law_of_universal_gravitation)
    ForceOn(self: PointGravity, body: RigidBody3D): Vector3D
    {
        var toCentre = body.Pose.Position.Between(self.Center);
        var distanceSquared = toCentre.MagnitudeSquared;
        var magnitude = self.GravitationalParameter * body.MassProperties.Mass.Amount
            * body.GravityScale / distanceSquared;
        return distanceSquared <= 0.0 ? Vector3D.Zero : toCentre.Normalize * magnitude;
    }
```

## Line 145

**Source:** [stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato, line 145](../../../../../stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato#L145).

```plato

    // Drag opposing motion: -(linear * v + quadratic * |v| * v). The linear term
    // dominates at low speed (Stokes) and the quadratic one at high speed
    // (form drag); carrying both lets one model cover the whole range.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_(physics))
    ForceOn(self: DragModel, body: RigidBody3D): Vector3D
    {
        var v = body.LinearVelocity;
        return v.Negative * (self.LinearCoefficient + self.QuadraticCoefficient * v.Magnitude);
    }
```
